## Load the data

```{r load-data}
#| eval: true
# load the data
trans.prob.mat = readRDS(url("https://sta323-fa26.github.io/data/trans-prob-mat.rds"))
cipher_text = readLines("https://sta323-fa26.github.io/data/ciphertext.txt")
```

Here is a secret message to decrypt:

```{r}
cipher_text
```

To score different keys, we have constructed a frequency table from all the 2-tuples of characters in the book *War and Peace* by Leo Tolstoy. The result is a data frame, `trans.prob.mat`, loaded in the code chunk above. We include the whitespace character as a 27th character in our alphabet. The row denotes the first English letter in a 2 character sequence while columns determine the second letter in the character sequence.

## Exercise 2

Explain what the function below does.

```{r}
#| label: score-function
 
score <- function(decoded) {
  logprob <- 0
  prevletter <- "SPACE"
  for (i in 1:nchar(decoded)) {
    curletter <- substring(decoded, i, i)
    if(curletter == " ") {
      curletter <- "SPACE"
    }
    logprob <- logprob + log(trans.prob.mat[rownames(trans.prob.mat) == prevletter,
                                             colnames(trans.prob.mat) == curletter])
    prevletter <- curletter
  }
  return(logprob)
} 
```
